utterances.text: We cannot think of this in any other way than it being Basara's personal position and he wrote that - we saw it on the first page - when he already retired. I did not find this to be incorporated into any official position, order, instruction, direction, and that the brigade behaved in this way. Why Basara, once he retired, wrote this in this way, that is now more a question for him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, we will ask him when he comes here because he's on the witness list. And just for the record, I'm sure you recall he retired at the end of 1992, not some late date. And as for this being his personal opinion, he was the commander and he wrote this as the war record. So it's not just a personal opinion, right; it's his history?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is perhaps his working notebook that he was keeping, but it's not a war diary. A war diary is a formatted work that is maintained by the command of the unit, not by the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I understand that. That's not what I'm saying this is. It's obviously not that. It says "war record" on the top. I'll move on to one last question on the last part of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If we could go to the Serbian page 5, page 3 of the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If you look at number 6, which is circled: "With the recognition of BH by Europe, war broke out between the Serbs and the Croats and Muslims, and the JNA withdrew from the territory of BH. The 6th left the forces of the JNA and became the Army of Republika Srpska. Its tasks changed, and then the Muslims and Croats became adversaries and the brigade was given the task of disarming them, preventing the slaughter of the Serbian people. The 6th then prepared the way for the seizure of power and secured the take-over of the territory and the municipalities of Sanski Most and Kljuc. The villages of Hrustovo and Vrhpolje put up resistance. Our units successfully cleared those areas." So Basara tells us in this that -- his record, that the sole purpose was not to make the area peaceful and safer; it was also to defend the Serb people from slaughter, to arm Serbs and only Serbs, to disarm Muslims and Croats, and prepare for the seizure of power. That's what the 6th Krajina Brigade was doing, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That is not correct. The 6th Brigade arrived in Sanski Most because it had been mobilised in the area in the first place. It was its base territory. That brigade was supposed to be there. I didn't find a single order, a single document where the 6th Sana Brigade would be asked to disarm only Muslims and Croats; rather, that brigade is ordered to collect the weapons illegally owned by the population, irrespective of their ethnicity. Second of all, Basara says here that he created conditions for the arrival of the Serbian authorities in the area, which is not correct. The authorities were established after the multi-party elections and continued to exist. That local government had members from the Croatian and Muslim ethnic groups in Sanski Most. At that moment, there was nobody who wanted to establish some new authorities, which means that it is not correct that conditions were being created for some take-over. It is true that the 6th Brigade had a task to protect the Serbian population in view of the fact that in the previous two world wars they suffered at the hand of their neighbours: Croats and Muslims. There are entire areas that had faired badly in the previous wars. That brigade was tasked with preventing inter-ethnic conflicts and with disarming those who had illegal weapons. Everybody was entitled to possess arms legally because nobody made a distinction between ethnic groups, to say that only certain ethnicities would be members of the brigade. Before the conflict broke out in the former Yugoslavia, the 6th Brigade had members from the Croat and Muslim ethnic groups in proportion with their representation in the general population. Nobody prevented them from participating in the tasks that the brigade was supposed to carry out according to the plan of the former JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. So we'll move along, but is your testimony then that in Sanski Most, the 6th Krajina Brigade disarmed Muslims, Croats, and Serbs equally? And they didn't just disarm Muslims and Croats. Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I'm saying is that the brigade's task was to collect, or rather, to seize all the illegal weapons that existed at the time. I'm not saying that an equal numbers -- number was disarmed because the Serbs responded to mobilisation and were issued with weapons legally in the unit, whereas, at the same time, the Muslims and Croats didn't respond to mobilisation and most of them did not possess their weapons legally.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Let me stop you there and we're going to move to the issue of the moving out of the population which you discuss in your report at page 24, where you say in the newly arisen situation, living together was impossible and the resettlement and separation was in no doubt one of the options. You stand by that, living together was impossible? That's your view of the situation in Bosnia-Herzegovina in 1992? Let's say April/May 1992.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is my position and this is how it was when you couldn't live in a state as the former Yugoslavia had been. That state was much more comfortable for everybody. And when a peaceful solution could not be found - Bosnia and Herzegovina was in the same boat - people had to lose their rights, some of the people had to lose their rights in order to provide for conditions for the people living together. There was no good solution for Bosnia and Herzegovina. All the documents show that and those documents are of political nature and they will tell you that the Serbs kept on searching for a peaceful solution; however, they didn't find understanding on the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- Bosnia and Herzegovina is still burdened with --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Let me stop you because we'll move on and be able to explain more of that when we get to the area I'm moving to. When you were here in this case earlier, you testified at 40945 to 40946, you criticised

utterances.speaker: MR. BROWN SAYING
utterances.text: "Muslims and Croats moved out and Mr. Brown treats this in his findings as forcible departure. In some paragraphs he also refers to that as ethnic cleansing which was done under the pressure put on them to bear by the Serbian authorities and that was the key and main reason why the population decided to move out." And then you go on to say: "What I find to be really significant and what I deem to be significant is the fact that the population mostly moved out because of the fact that in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina, a conflict had started, a war had started, and there was a state of insecurity that reigned and everybody tried to leave the area if they could do that," et cetera. So your thesis is that there was no forced departure of Muslims and Croats. They just moved out because, like all people, they were scared of the war and left areas of combat; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in 1992 Bosnia-Herzegovina was divided. Its territory was divided between the three peoples. According to the principle of ethnic majority. Each of the peoples under those conditions tried or at least wanted to go to a place where they would be safer or where they thought that they would be safer, and they thought that they would be safer where they were a majority and where they could exercise their rights. That was the essence of their departure. Everybody left, everybody moved out, not only Muslims and Croats. Not only the two ethnicities moved out from the territory of Republika Srpska. The Serbs also moved out from the territory of the Muslim Federation or the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina as it was called at the time --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- both Muslims and Serbs moved out from Herceg-Bosnia so that --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. And that includes Sanski Most, right, that analysis? If you could answer that "yes" or "no." You say people weren't forced to leave from Sanski Most, Muslims and Croats?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my report I mention a lot of documents issued by Mr. Karadzic, the Main Staff of the army, 1 KK, the civilian authorities. And those documents show that they insisted that no pressure should be put to bear on the population, forcing them to move out. They were encouraged to choose freely where they would live. What they were requested to do was to comply with the authorities that had been legally elected in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. Let me show you P03645 very quickly. These are the Sanski Most Crisis Staff inclusions. This is 7th of May, 1992, item 1: "The Crisis Staff of the Sanski Most Serbian Municipality shall operate as a War Staff as of today. "Crisis Staff is ... exclusively used in public. "2. Mladen Lukic and Mirko Vrucinic shall hold talks with the Commander of the 6th Krajina Brigade, Colonel Basara, to get him involved as a member of the War Staff of the Sanski Most Serbian Municipality and to agree on transforming the JNA into the Serbian Territorial Defence." So this is even before the 16th Assembly Session, but you will agree the Crisis Staff is reaching out, operating secretly as a war staff, to get Basara more involved; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were individual attempts, like in Sanski Most, to have the army unit placed under the local government. You will see it in the findings that the situation was very similar in Kljuc. However, the armed forces and the system of command was strictly regulated and it is based on the principle of the unity of command and singleness of command. All the units are under a single command. It was not possible or at least I did not find a single document which would show that that conclusion was ever implemented, that the staff and whatever it may be called, a Crisis Staff or the war staff, ever placed that unit under its command. I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yeah, and I wasn't saying they were placed under its command. It was under the command of General Talic, but he was becoming involved with the war staff; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Crisis Staffs, or rather, a war staff as an institution does not exist. You will not find it in the rules, regulations, laws, acts, anywhere. There were staffs for extraordinary situations, but not war staffs. A Crisis Staff is a form of institutionalised action in an area, usually a municipality, that unifies all incumbents and all those who are interested in overcoming the war situation in the easiest possible way. One of its members is the commander of a military unit or the commander of the Territorial Defence. It is possible and it is true that they probably asked for the brigade commander to become a Crisis Staff member.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Are we stopping at quarter to, Your Honour? One more quick document then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: -- hopefully quick. P02613.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: It's a Crisis Staff decision, 22nd of May, from their meeting on the 21st of May. And it begins: "On the basis of a proclamation by the president of the Presidency of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Dr. Radovan Karadzic, the Crisis Staff of Sanski Most will implement the decision on general mobilisation of forces and equipment in the republic and hereby issues the following instructions to that effect ..." "(d) the commander of the 6th Krajina Brigade, Colonel Basara, and the commander of the Serbian Territorial Defence, Colonel Anicic, are hereby instructed to protect vital facilities in the town, above all the water supply system, the transformer, the silos, et cetera."

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If we can go to the next page in English. "4. As far as disarming paramilitary formations in Sanski Most is concerned, Colonel Basara and Colonel Anicic are charged with putting this into practice: "(a) the final dead-line for handing in weapons is 2000 hours on 24 May 1992." And then in subparagraph (b), it talks about trying to ensure peace in Sanski Most and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: This document shows that, in fact, the civilian authorities, Rasula and Vrkes, are working with the 6th Krajina Brigade commander, Basara, with the TO, Anicic, in order to prepare combat activities; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is not about combat activities. This is about the control of the territory and protection of the infrastructure in the territory. Army units can be engaged on those tasks together with the police units and the Territorial Defence units.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: It's about them disarming together; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of the tasks would be disarming, or rather, insisting on weapons being returned within a certain dead-line. We did that as well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours, that's a good time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We'll adjourn for today and continue tomorrow morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 25th day of July, 2013, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.47 p.m.,
